title: Push Dominoes
summary: Given a string representing the initial state of n dominoes, where each domino is either pushed to the left ('L'), pushed to the right ('R'), or standing upright ('.'), simulate the domino effect over time.
statement: Given a string representing the initial state of n dominoes, where each domino is either pushed to the left ('L'), pushed to the right ('R'), or standing upright ('.'), simulate the domino effect over time. Each second, any upright domino between two falling dominoes remains still due to the balance of forces. Return the final state of the dominoes as a string.
constraints: L and R exert one unit of force per time step; equal opposing forces leave a domino upright.
hints: Only the nearest non-dot forces bounding a dot interval determine its outcome.
Add neutral sentinels and resolve each interval by endpoint directions.
Equal forces fill the gap; L...R stays upright; R...L fills inward with optional center dot.
More distant forces are blocked by the interval endpoints, so intervals can be solved independently.
editorial: More distant forces are blocked by the interval endpoints, so intervals can be solved independently.

tests.explanation: The existing dot is balanced against no new force, so RR.L remains unchanged.
Resolving each interval between forces yields LL.RR.LLRRLL..
